To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned and characterized four genes that are involved in the delivery of endosomes and lysosomes.
the human homologs VPS18, -11, -16, and -33 are all expressed in a variety of human tissues.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the human orthologues of the four genes of the yeast vacuolar protein sorting (vps) pathway.
the molecular characterization of the class C Vps genes and their role in the pathogenesis in Hermansky-Podlak syndrome.
the molecular basis of human diseases that affect the function of the lysosomal system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VPS18 gene product, a protein of unknown function, is a novel component of the ESCRT-III complex and that VPS11 and VPS16 are novel components of the ESCRT-I complex.
the human Vps18, Vps11, Vps16, and Vps33 genes have been cloned and their expression patterns characterized.
the VPS18, 11, 16, and 33 genes are expressed in human tissues, and that their expression pattern is consistent with the known cellular functions of the yeast homologs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified four genes that are homologous to yeast vacuolar protein sorting genes.

we have cloned and characterized the human homologs for yeast VPS18, 11, 16, and 33, and that the expression of all four genes is restricted to the hematopoietic lineage, and that they may be involved in lysosome-related organelle biogenesis.

we identified four novel human cDNAs that share sequence similarity with the yeast class C vacuolar protein sorting genes VPS18, 11, 16, and 33, and we show that the expression of these cDNAs is ubiquitous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VPS18, the gene that is mutated in Hermansky-Putlak syndrome type 3, is ubiquitously expressed.
the human homologs are expressed in many tissues and in some tissues, the four class c vps homologs are coexpressed.
VPS18, the human homolog of yeast vps18, is expressed ubiquitously, and is highly conserved in its sequence, with the exception of a 12-residue insertion.
